intended_object: An auxiliary step in building the localized adjunction G' ⊣ F' between localized categories (`Adjunction.localization`). It is the would-be counit F' ⋙ G' ⟶ 𝟭 D₂. This comes from the docstring ("Auxiliary definition of the counit morphism for the adjunction `Adjunction.localization`").
explanation: The docstring says this is an auxiliary definition used to build `Adjunction.localization`. The intended mathematical object is that adjunction (and its counit), not this standalone construction. The construction itself makes sense: it lifts the whiskered counit `L₂ ∘ ε : (F ⋙ G) ⋙ L₂ ⟶ L₂` along the localization functor L₂. To do so it uses `liftNatTrans`, with the identification (F ⋙ G) ⋙ L₂ ≅ L₂ ⋙ (F' ⋙ G') given by the composed commutative squares. That is the standard way to get the counit of the induced adjunction on localizations. Still, it is an internal building block of a proof or construction, so it is best classed as a technical device rather than a standalone mathematical definition.
